_meta.purpose: Frozen criterion list for the §5.1 judgement oracle. ORACLE=JUDGE rows only -- everything ORACLE=STATIC or TOOLING is handled by deterministic rules/rcmdcheck instead, per the ledger's own priority order (tooling -> static -> judge).
_meta.prov_note: criterion-corpus.md tags PROV explicitly per row. criterion-corpus-longtail.md has no PROV column -- it is described in its own header as findings 'scraped from cran-comments.md files, GitHub issue threads, and r-package-devel archives', i.e. by construction not derivable from the frozen handbook snapshot every arm received. All longtail rows are therefore inferred as COMMUNITY here; this inference is recorded, not silently assumed.
_meta.letter_note: No JUDGE-oracle row is tagged LETTER in either corpus file -- both real orthoMTL findings (R01, R02) are ORACLE=STATIC, so the judge carries zero of the two known ground-truth findings.
_meta.l23_c18_overlap_note: C18 (HANDBOOK) and L23 (COMMUNITY, inferred) both concern \dontrun{} legitimacy and substantially overlap in content -- L23 gives the concrete 5-second/--run-dontrun threshold, C18 is the general handbook statement. Kept as two separate frozen rows per the source tables rather than merged post-hoc; scored independently.

criteria.text: Description is an elaborated paragraph, not one line
Method/API references cited as doi:, arXiv:, ISBN: or URL
Maintainer email address is appropriate and durable
\dontrun{} only where the example genuinely cannot run -- missing software, API keys
Every acronym must be expanded in Description (e.g. X-SAMPA, BPMN, GWAS, SNP)
Double quotes reserved for publication titles; not used for emphasis or ordinary phrases
Description names/describes the main wrapper function instead of describing the package as a whole
Description is too thin -- needs more detail about functionality and implemented methods
References section present when the package implements a published method (a strong suggestion, requested on most new submissions)
Version number reflects package maturity (not artificially inflated for a first submission)
\dontrun{} used only where genuinely unrunnable; an example completing in under ~5s under --run-dontrun should be \donttest{} or unwrapped
Example datasets are appropriately small -- examples exist to show call syntax, not to demonstrate scale
